Prefer to read? The walkthrough in words, and what RoofMap is in plain terms

Draw the roof. Type the address and RoofMap loads the aerial photo and sets the scale from it. Click the corners of the building; walls snap square, and the ridges, hips and valleys are worked out from the outline and the pitch. Every edge is measured as you go.

Generate the job pack. The same drawing becomes the sheet layout for every plane, the cut list, the flashing schedule and the fixings — and shows where the hip offcuts come from. It goes to the crew as a PDF they can read on the roof.

The customer picks an option. The quote is a six-page proposal with the roof plan on it. The customer chooses steel grade, gauge, guttering or whether the garage is in, watches the total move, and accepts from their phone. You are told the moment they open it and the moment they accept.

Send the material order. Quantities are counted off the drawing and the order goes to your merchant with one button. Linked to Fergus, the job pack goes back to the Fergus job as well.

Who it is for
Australian roofing businesses quoting metal roofing: one estimator, or an office and several crews.
What you enter
A site address, the traced outline of the roof, the pitch, and your own supplier rates and labour.
What it produces
A measured roof plan, sheet cut lists and a flashing schedule, a merchant material order, a customer quote accepted online, and invoices.
Do you need Fergus?
No. RoofMap runs on its own. If you use Fergus, jobs and photos come across and the job pack goes back.

On the roof

The measuring app goes up the ladder with you.

This is the part most quoting software doesn't have. Draw the roof on your phone or tablet while you're standing on it — and every ridge, hip, valley, barge and gutter is measured as you go, ready for the office before you're back in the ute.

  • Finger or pen, gloves on. Big targets, no fiddly menus, and it ignores your palm resting on the screen.
  • Lock the screen. One tap and the roof can't be redrawn by your leg while the phone's in your pocket.
  • Photos into the job. Shoot the whole roof in one go — every shot lands on the job, not in your camera roll.
  • No signal, no problem. It saves to the device and uploads itself the moment you have coverage.
  • The office picks it straight up. Site drafts arrive named and stamped with who measured it and on what.
Who built it

Written by roofers, on real jobs.

RoofMap came out of a working roofing company in Northland, New Zealand. It was built because quoting a re-roof took an afternoon of tape measures and spreadsheets, and because the material order was never quite right.

Every feature in it earned its place on a real job first. That's why the cut lists match how a roof is actually laid, and why the app works with one hand on a windy roof.

  • Priced and ordered on live re-roofs, not demo data
  • Your own steel, profiles and gutters set up once — COLORBOND®, ZINCALUME®, CUSTOM ORB®, TRIMDEK®, Quad gutter or whatever you sell
  • Your supplier's prices and your labour rates, with GST on your customer quotes at the rate you set

COLORBOND®, ZINCALUME®, LYSAGHT®, CUSTOM ORB®, TRIMDEK®, KLIP-LOK® and SPANDEK® are registered trade marks of BlueScope Steel Limited.

Pricing

Priced per business, not per seat.

Measure the roof, calculate your materials, export your pricing, and get back to running the business. Your estimator, your office manager and your foreman all work off the same jobs, the same price book and the same job numbers.

Measuring is included on every plan, with no per-roof fee. Per-report measuring services charge roughly A$35–$60 a roof to measure it for you — twenty roofs a month is A$700 to $1,200 before you have priced anything.
